title: Coboundary expanders of bounded degree
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Coboundary expansion is the property of a simplicial complex that a set of faces with a small coboundary, over the field with two elements, is close to a coboundary; for graphs it is edge expansion. The first lesson defines cochains, weights and norms, proves that a coboundary expander has no cohomology below its dimension, that the full simplex and the complete complexes are coboundary expanders, and that an expansion inequality passes to a skeleton with a controlled constant. It states the theorem of OpenAI (2026): in every dimension at least three there are arbitrarily large coboundary expanders with a common constant in which every vertex lies in a bounded number of faces. The second lesson studies coset complexes of an arbitrary group with a family of subgroups: the faces of a type are the cosets of the intersection of the subgroups of that type, the complex is pure and the group acts transitively on the faces of each type, it is connected exactly when the subgroups generate the group, and the coset complex of a quotient group is the quotient complex when the intersections are preserved. The third lesson defines the complexes: groups of polynomial matrices generated by elementary matrices attached to the edges of a cycle, described exactly by the pattern of their entries; the group of polynomial matrices of determinant one that are upper unitriangular at zero is generated by them (proved by commutators and the Euclidean algorithm); the coset complexes of its quotients modulo powers of t and their skeletons are finite, pure and connected, with a bounded number of faces at every vertex and a number of vertices that tends to infinity. The theorem on coboundary expansion is derived from two named statements about these complexes: an expansion inequality relative to the cocycles, and the vanishing of their cohomology. The two named statements are theorems of the literature and of OpenAI's text that this course does not prove.
prerequisites: core course Linear Algebra (B40): vector spaces over a field, here the field with two elements
core course Abstract Algebra I (C30): groups, subgroups, cosets, normal subgroups, quotient groups
core course Linear Algebra (B40): matrices over a commutative ring, determinants; division with remainder for polynomials over a field
the lessons prove every other fact they use

checks.reading: Lesson 1 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Section 1 (definitions, the statement of the theorem) and the subsection 'Weights on skeleta' of Section 5 of OpenAI's manuscript 'Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension' (24 Sep 2026); all five sections of the manuscript were read before. Every step of the lesson was derived; the cone argument for the full simplex and the corollary for complete complexes are not in the manuscript and are standard. The attributions in Section 6 (Chapman and Lubotzky; Linial, Meshulam, Wallach; Gromov; Oppenheim and Valentiner-Branth) are taken from the manuscript's introduction; those works were not read. Lesson 2 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the definition of coset complexes in Section 2 of the manuscript and the uses made of it in Sections 3 to 5 (faces of a type as cosets of the intersection, the count of chambers through a face, connectedness and generation in the proof of the corollary on generation, the quotient by the congruence subgroup in the proposition on homology comparisons); the statements are formulated for arbitrary groups and proved. A first draft of Exercise 4.2 asserted an exact count that holds only as an upper bound; the exercise now asks for the bound, and a first draft of the solution of Exercise 4.3 miscounted the edges of the quotient; both were corrected before staging. Lesson 3 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Section 2, the lemma on patterns and the corollary on generation of Section 3, and the subsections on degree bounds and on the proof of the theorem of Section 5 of the manuscript. The pattern lemma is proved in full (the manuscript sketches it). The generation of U by the simple root elements is proved by an elementary argument (commutators along walks on the cycle; the Euclidean algorithm on the first column), which replaces the manuscript's proof through the connectedness of the building model; it needs N >= 3. Checked by enumeration (plan/checks_20261012/ce_check_generation.py) for (N, q, m) = (3, 2, 2), (3, 3, 2), (3, 2, 3), (4, 2, 2): the orders of the H_i, of H_0 n H_1, the trivial total intersection, and the order of the group generated by all x_i modulo t^m, which equals the order of the image of U. A draft exercise asserted that for N = 2, q = 3 the two generators do not generate e_12(t); the enumeration modulo t^2 and t^3 (ce_check_n2.py) does not support any such statement at finite level, and the exercise was replaced before staging. Theorem 4.1 derives the main theorem from the statements (E) and (V); no gap found in the manuscript's Sections 2 and 5 and in the elementary parts of Section 3; Sections 3 (building model) and 4 (homology) were read but not checked step by step.

open_obligations: Hypothesis without a provider in the programme: statement (E) of lesson 3, the expansion inequality relative to the cocycles for the skeletons of dimension 2d - 1 of the complexes T_m, with a constant independent of m. The manuscript takes it from Theorem 1.2 of Oppenheim and Valentiner-Branth on Kac-Moody-Steinberg complexes, for q large enough; that theorem and the verification that the T_m are such complexes (their definitions) were not read in the original.

Hypothesis without a provider in the programme: statement (V) of lesson 3, H^i(T_m; F_2) = 0 for 1 <= i <= d - 1. The manuscript proves it in its Sections 3 and 4 with: the affine twin building of SL_N(k[t, 1/t]) and codistance; the contractibility of affine buildings; the acyclicity of spherical opposition complexes (Oppenheim and Valentiner-Branth); homology of groups (projective resolutions from an acyclic complex with stabilizers of odd order, coinvariants, transfer, universal coefficients); Morrow's pro Tor-unitality theorem and Iwasa's homology pro-stability theorem; a stable range computation for the ideals t^m k[t]. These sections were read; they are not written as lessons because the foundations are missing in the programme (mailbox C-0257).

With (E) and (V) as hypotheses, Theorem 4.1 of lesson 3 gives OpenAI's main theorem for every d >= 1 for which the hypotheses hold; the manuscript establishes them for d >= 3 and odd primes q that are large enough.
free_sources: OpenAI, Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension (OpenAI Math Release preprint, 24 Sep 2026), Sections 1, 2, 5 and the elementary parts of Section 3
